Where the files in this directory come from. All of them are answers of running software,
captured on 2026-11-18/19 on a Fedora 43 workstation with curl over the runtime's unix socket.
Fields the collector does not read were dropped with jq to keep the files small and free of
the machine's paths; no value was changed except where noted.

podman/   Podman 5.8.9, rootless, "podman system service" on a socket of its own.
          The containers were made for the capture:
            upkeep-fx-autoupdate  alpine:3.20, label io.containers.autoupdate=registry
            upkeep-fx-digest      docker.io/library/alpine@sha256:d9e853... (no tag)
            upkeep-fx-local       localhost/upkeep-fixture:current, built on the machine
            upkeep-fx-inpod       alpine:3.20, inside the pod upkeep-fx-pod
            5b4d509f88e5-infra    that pod's infra container (it has no image)
            upkeep-fx-exited      ran "true" and ended
            upkeep-fx-created     created, never started
  ping.txt                  GET /_ping with headers (curl -i); the X-Reference-Id header removed
  containers.json           GET /containers/json?all=true, the seven containers above
  container-<id>.json       GET /containers/<name>/json
  image-<id>.json           GET /images/<id>/json                  (Docker's API as Podman serves it)
  libpod-image-<id>.json    GET /v5.8.9/libpod/images/<id>/json    (Podman's own API)
  missing-container.json    GET /containers/1111...1111/json            -> 404
  missing-image.json        GET /images/sha256:1111...1111/json         -> 404
  status-filter-refused.json  GET /containers/json?filters={"status":["running","restarting"]} -> 500;
                            why the collector lists everything and filters itself

  Of alpine's two RepoDigests, sha256:d9e853... is the multi-architecture index the tag pointed
  at and sha256:c64c68... the amd64 image inside it (checked with "skopeo inspect --raw").

podman-debian13/   Podman 5.4.2 as Debian 13 packages it (5.4.2+ds1-2+b2), run inside a
          debian:trixie container with its API service on a socket there; the same calls and
          the same trimming as above. version.txt is "podman --version" and dpkg-query.
            fx-autoupdate         alpine:3.20, label io.containers.autoupdate=registry
            fx-inpod              alpine:3.20, inside the pod fx-pod
            f24c1881aa0c-infra    that pod's infra container; in this version it has an image,
                                  localhost/podman-pause:5.4.2-1766335321

docker/   Docker Engine 29.9.2 (API 1.56, containerd image store), the workstation's own daemon,
          read only. Seven of its containers were picked; the names of the owner's projects in
          container and image names were replaced (shop-*, logs-*, app-engine*, cache-*), and of
          the labels only com.docker.compose.service was kept.
  ping.txt                  GET /_ping with headers
  containers.json           GET /containers/json?all=true&filters={"name":[...]}
  container-<id>.json       GET /containers/<id>/json
  image-<id>.json           GET /images/<id>/json
  missing-image.json        GET /images/sha256:284e08.../json -> 404. This is the image of the
                            running container shop-db: its tag was rebuilt, the old image is gone.
                            The same container is listed with the image ID in place of a name.
  missing-container.json    GET /containers/nonexistent/json -> 404

The test cases that say so in their names change one field of a capture (a state, an image
name) for situations that could not be captured.
